column6: Simulator inference runs on the host Mac; an Xcode 27 SDK on macOS 26 manufactures error -1 that looks like your bug.
A schema flag that fails to apply still yields prose on stdout with exit 0; jq errors lines later, blaming the wrong stage.
The instrument's trace file is a sensitive artefact: it captures prompt and response data in the clear.
No one on this project ran Xcode 27's Instruments; four of six timeline lanes are unverified — UI claims trace to narration.
A tool named in instructions but missing from the toolset loops the model: fluent wrong-mode output and no error.
The code-along targets macOS Tahoe/Xcode 26 — treat its Playground UI details as 'at least true in 26', not 27.
Simulator inference runs on the host Mac's OS; version-skew errors surface as a bare -1 that reads as your bug.
LanguageModelFeedback attachments carry the full session transcript — consent, no auto-upload, scrub before sharing.
Menu strings differ between Apple's spoken narration and its written docs — don't pattern-match one exact wording.
One availability branch is contaminated by a confirmed Apple bug — do not design around it.
availability returns .appleIntelligenceNotEnabled unless Siri is enabled, even with AI on — Apple-confirmed bug.
Recording a trace turns FM logging on; read the Record Anyway dialog before clicking.
Starting a trace enables prompt/response capture in the clear for the recording — get consent and scrub before sharing.
The canonical bug: instructions name a tool the toolset lacks; the model loops in brainstorm mode, output stays plausible.
Captions spell the idea tool three ways (GenerateCraftIdeaTool/IdeasTool/generateCraftIdea); the exact name is unverified.
Every layer behaves correctly while the user sees the wrong feature — the model can't switch modes and nothing throws.
The model kept accepting input and making tool calls, never threw, and gave no signal — Apple's archetypal silent failure.
includeSchemaInPrompt: false without a one-shot example leaves neither schema nor pattern — structured output degrades.
A turn that is only a tool call completes streamResponse with zero partials; spinner-until-first-partial UIs hang forever.
Session 242 defers cache-invalidation detection to 243, which never mentions it; cache hit rate exists only in written docs.
Linear-attention/hybrid models forfeit prefix caching and re-prefill each turn; the 101x TTFT gain is attention-only.
The transcript-recorder JSON files contain the full transcript — apply the same consent and scrubbing rules before sharing.
capabilities claims vision and tool calling on the 27.0 sim where both fail at runtime; it is a declaration, not a health check
The coffee-game and SpeechAnalyzer samples are iOS 26-era harvests — do not read them as evidence of 27 behaviour.
Evidence in this guide is the weakest of Parts 1-6 — read the provenance warning before trusting details.
TOC: memory across the Python/Swift boundary — fd leaks after ~240 image calls, retained attachments, double-free crashes.
A community post argues fm serve does not exist from its absence in a transcript; an Apple engineer and a --help paste say otherwise.
fmx is a third-party macOS 26 look-alike; its slash commands and flags are its own design and read as attested fm surface.
fm respond writes prose to stdout when a schema isn't applied, exit 0; jq errors later naming the wrong culprit.
apple_fm_sdk.__version__ is hardcoded 0.1.0 on a 0.2.1 package; capability checks keyed on it test a constant.
The Python SDK is 26-generation (macOS 26+) though the session is about macOS 27 throughout — expect capability gaps.
The SDK runs on macOS 26 but the fm CLI does not exist there — the session presents them as one workflow.
The Python SDK exposes no 27-era surface: no PCC (none planned — shell out to fm), no reasoning, no attachments.
Image support is compiled in or out by the build machine's macOS SDK; users learn only when an image prompt fails.
A wheel built where SDK detection returns None or <27 omits image support; nothing at runtime says so until a prompt fails.
pytest outside the repo root fails on FileNotFoundError for fixtures — it reads like a broken install and is not.
The docstring's SystemLanguageModel(temperature:top_p:) raises TypeError — sampling lives on GenerationOptions.
token_count([]) takes the tools path (vacuous all()) and returns the empty toolset's count, not a prompt count.
In the generating=Cat branch of respond, your options are dropped.
respond(generating:options:) silently discards options — session.py:473 calls _respond_with_schema without them.
_stream_response skips the session request lock every respond path takes; a stream and respond() interleave unserialised.
top_k/top_p/seed are serialised as strings the Swift side fails to cast — sampling is never assigned; seeds do nothing.
GuideType members are camelCase (maxItems) while factories are snake_case (max_items) — an autocomplete trap.
Optionality is substring-sniffed from the type string — 'int | None' fields silently become required.
is_optional is 'Optional' in str(type): int | None never matches, and Optional[int] stops matching on Python 3.14.
The @fm.generable description is stored and never read — the type-level description never reaches the model.
@fm.generable('desc') stores _generable_description; nothing passes it into the schema — grep finds zero readers.
value(int, for_property:) never coerces raw values — the coercion helper is dead code and a JSON string stays a str.
The Swift/Python parity fixtures differ (Int .range vs prose-bounded nested type) — parity is schema-level only.
Exceptions raised inside a tool's call() never reach your except block — they are stringified and fed to the model.
A tool exception becomes 'Tool error: ...' handed to the model; respond() succeeds and the caller never sees it.
A tool call() that never returns leaves the Swift continuation unresumed — the session hangs forever, no timeout, no error.
Tool validation is bare asserts, disabled under python -O — a tool missing description fails later and less legibly.
ImageAttachment path must be pathlib.Path; a plain str dies on path.is_file() with AttributeError, not a friendly error.
Prompts expand any non-str iterable: a consumed generator retries as an empty prompt; a dict contributes only its keys.
Image input is unreliable for spatial localisation — confident answers that misplace regions (thread 838613).
Transcript-loaded tools are historical only; forget to re-pass instances and the replayed session can never call tools.
Transcripts are user words: exporting them off-device is a data-collection decision — consent, redaction, retention.
Native memory and fds cross the Python/Swift boundary — batches leak unless sessions are recreated and releases run.
pip's apple-fm-sdk 0.2.1 still has the image fd leak; the fix landed 2026-07-07 on git main only — install from main.
Manual cleanup of native session resources crashes the interpreter — never call the internal _release() yourself.
session._release() double-frees when GC releases again — EXC_BREAKPOINT/SIGTRAP in libswiftCore.dylib.
pytest collects test_memory_stress.py and runs nothing — it defines no test_ functions; invoke it with python directly.
test_composed_prompt_cleanup.py's docstring promises an fd-count regression test; the file has only four mocked unit tests.
except fm.FoundationModelsError misses image failures — PromptError/ImagePromptError subclass plain Exception; catch both.
Reproducible sampling is greedy-only in Python — random-sampling params, seed included, never survive the bridge.
Symptom-to-cause table of the SDK's non-throwing failures: dropped options, failed seed casts, ignored guides, hung tools.
